sections.h2: Who sends and collects Sibley County property tax bills?
sections.html:
The Auditor-Treasurer sends and collects the bills, and the Assessor decides what each parcel is worth. Both offices work out of the courthouse at 400 Court Avenue in Gaylord. The Auditor-Treasurer is on the first floor of the historic courthouse at 507-237-4070 (mail to P.O. Box 51, Gaylord, MN 55334). The Assessor is on the second floor at 507-237-4078, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 to 4:30, with mail going to P.O. Box 532.

The Assessor's page is plain about the split: questions about your tax or special assessments belong with the Auditor-Treasurer, while value and class belong to the Assessor. Copies of the current value notice and tax statement can be pulled from the county's online tax portal, or either office can send you a copy.

sections.h2: What is Sibley County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Sibley County is a rural county in south central Minnesota, with Gaylord as its seat and largest city. It covers 601 square miles, with 589 of them land, and the terrain is rolling hills cut by creeks and dotted with small lakes. The Minnesota River forms the eastern border, and most of the Rush River watershed lies inside the county. Farmland takes up much of the map.

The first county seat was Henderson, where a courthouse opened in 1879. Gaylord took over in 1915 after residents petitioned the supervisors, and the old building now holds the Henderson city offices. Other cities are Arlington, Gibbon, Green Isle, New Auburn and Winthrop, along with part of Le Sueur. Census QuickFacts gives these markers:

  • 15,356 residents in July 2025, up 3.4% from the 2020 base
  • 6,596 housing units, 80.8% of them lived in by the owner
  • Median owner-occupied value of $231,900 and median gross rent of $855
  • Median household income of $77,634, with 21.7% of residents aged 65 or older
  • 28 building permits in 2025, and a mean commute of 27.1 minutes

The permit count is small next to the housing stock, so most homes that change hands here are existing houses.

sections.h2: When are Sibley County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The first half of real estate tax is due May 15, and the second half is due October 15 for residential and commercial parcels. Agricultural parcels pay the second half by November 15. A mailed payment must be postmarked by the due date, and a Saturday or Sunday due date moves to the next business day.

Sibley County due dates by tax type (county Current Year Taxes page)
Type of taxFirst paymentSecond payment
Residential or commercial real estateMay 15October 15
Agricultural real estateMay 15November 15
Personal propertyMay 15, full amountNone
Mobile homeAugust 31November 15

A real estate bill of $100 or less is due in full on the first date, and the second stub on your statement will be blank. A mobile home bill under $50 is due in full August 31. Statements go out once a year, by the state's March 31 deadline, and the 2026 statements were mailed on March 20. The 2026 second-half date of October 15 has now passed, so check the portal for any balance still open on a parcel you plan to sell.

sections.h2: How do I pay a Sibley County tax bill?
sections.html:
The county asks owners to pay online or by mail when possible, and it asks that every stub be sent with the payment, because the office is not responsible for parcels left unpaid. Payments post by parcel ID number.

  • Card or e-check: 2.35% of the amount with a $1.50 minimum for cards, and a flat $1.50 for e-check. A phone option is 507-237-4070 in business hours or 855-414-3916 after hours.
  • Mail: use the return envelope and the P.O. Box 51 address. The county notes that the Postal Service now dates mail when it receives it, so it suggests mailing days early or asking for a manual postmark.
  • Drop box: a locked box at the courthouse west entrance is emptied at 8:00 each morning, and anything placed before 8:00 counts as the previous day.
  • Direct Payment Plan: free withdrawals on May 15 and October 15 or November 15, with sign-up requested at least three weeks ahead.

Partial payments are accepted at any time. The full half is still due on the due date, but penalty accrues only on what remains unpaid. A returned payment costs $30. An email reminder list sends a notice 10 to 14 days before each deadline, though the county states that late penalties apply whether or not you got one.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Sibley County valuation?
sections.html:
The path runs through a local board between April 1 and May 31, then the county board in June, with Tax Court as the last stop. The valuation is set as of January 2 each year, and the Assessor reviews sales from October 1 through September 30 of the prior year. Under the county's description, state guidelines expect the overall assessment level to land between 90% and 105% of sale price.

  • Local Board of Appeal and Equalization: township boards and city councils hear owners in April and May. The Assessor attends to present data but does not vote.
  • Open Book: some jurisdictions pass their appeal powers to the county, which handles cases more informally. If you and the Assessor cannot agree, the next stop is the County Board.
  • Tax Court: the county's assessment calendar gives April 30 as the last day to file a petition for a dispute that affects the current year's taxes.

The burden is on the owner. The board page says the assessor is presumed to have valued and classified the property properly, so bring comparable sales, an appraisal or repair estimates. A local board can raise or lower a value and change a class, but it cannot cut a whole township or city by more than 1%. A written decision usually follows within 10 days. State law calls for a physical look at each parcel at least once every five years, and a postcard announces a visit in the spring of that year.

sections.h2: How does homestead status affect a Sibley County sale?
sections.html:
Selling ends the homestead, and the Assessor's page requires you to say so within 30 days. The same duty applies if you or your spouse move out or your marital status changes. A late report can bring the correct tax plus an equal penalty, according to the county.

Buyers who will live in the house must file their own application with the Assessor by December 31 of the assessment year, and the county advises applying soon after purchase. A notice on the county home page repeats the December 31, 2026 deadline for this year. Applications go to the Assessor's office on Court Avenue or to P.O. Box 532, and the form requires a Social Security or ITIN number for each owner.

The county adds that a house that is rented, offered for sale or occupied by someone other than the owner becomes non-homestead for the next assessment year.

faqs.q: What are the property tax due dates in Sibley County?
faqs.a: May 15 for the first half, October 15 for second-half residential and commercial real estate, and November 15 for agricultural second halves. Personal property is due in full on May 15. Mobile homes pay August 31 and November 15.

faqs.q: Where is the Sibley County Assessor?
faqs.a: On the second floor of the courthouse at 400 Court Avenue, Gaylord, MN 55334. The phone is 507-237-4078, and the office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to pay Sibley County taxes by card?
faqs.a: The county charges 2.35% of the amount, with a $1.50 minimum, for a credit or debit card. An e-check carries a flat $1.50 fee. Paying by mail, drop box or the Direct Payment Plan avoids those fees.

faqs.q: When do Sibley County boards of appeal meet?
faqs.a: Local boards meet in townships and cities between April 1 and May 31, and the County Board of Appeal and Equalization follows in June. The dates are printed on your Notice of Valuation and Classification.

faqs.q: Do I have to tell Sibley County when I sell my homestead?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell the County Assessor within 30 days of the sale. Call 507-237-4078 if you need the form or have questions about your situation.
